title: Bear-and-bee FSP and concurrent Java project with ChatGPT
summary: Students model a producer-consumer problem in Finite State Processes, implement and test the model in concurrent Java, and use ChatGPT 3.5 for clarification and feedback. They submit the model, code, ChatGPT transcript, and an experience survey for bonus credit.

sources.title: Integrating Conversational Large Language Models into Student Learning: A Case Study of ChatGPT in Software Engineering Education

locator.section: III. The Design of the Study

sources.evidence_quote: The students were required to submit the designed FSP model for the problem, the Java source code that implemented the FSP model, the chat record with ChatGPT, and a completed survey of 10 questions.

context.discipline: formal methods and concurrent Java programming

course.name: CIS 461 Formal Methods for Software Engineering

context.learner_level: undergraduate and graduate computer science students

assessment.summary: Model the bear-and-bee producer-consumer problem in FSP, implement the model with concurrent Java constructs, and test the implementation.
student_actions: Ask ChatGPT for problem clarification and examples.
Develop and refine an FSP model.
Design, implement, and test a concurrent Java solution.
Evaluate ChatGPT responses rather than requesting direct implementation.

student_role.description: Students were encouraged to use ChatGPT 3.5 for clarification, model and design feedback, code feedback, and debugging.

grading.method: Modeling and implementation performance were scored; the department's satisfactory criterion was 80% of students earning at least 80/100 in each component.
